A legal battle involving prominent Nollywood figure Emeka Ike has reached a significant milestone in the nation's capital. The Federal High Court sitting in Abuja delivered a ruling on Wednesday, bringing an end to a major fundamental rights lawsuit brought forward by the veteran actor. According to reports, the legal action sought damages amounting to N10bn.

The respondent at the center of the legal challenge is Lere Olayinka, who serves as the Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications to Nyesom Wike, the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory. Alongside the FCT Minister's aide, the Independent National Electoral Commission was also named as a respondent in the proceedings initiated by the prominent entertainment figure.

Presiding over the matter, Justice Salim Ibrahim addressed the case by evaluating the legal arguments presented by the defense. The court ultimately decided to dismiss the high-stakes fundamental rights suit entirely. This decision came after the presiding judge sustained a preliminary objection raised against the continuation of the legal action.

While the dismissal marks a decisive chapter in the ongoing legal dynamics between the involved parties, further details regarding the core arguments of the preliminary objection remain closely tied to the court proceedings in Abuja.
